newsitem.title: FRANCE: French far-right leader eyes 1998 regional polls.
newsitem.headline: French far-right leader eyes 1998 regional polls.

text.p: French far-right leader Jean-Marie Le Pen said on Sunday that he would lead his National Front party in regional elections in southwest France next year.
He told reporters at a party conference in the Riviera capital of Nice that he would head his anti-immigration party's list in the Alpes-Maritimes department in early 1998.
He did not say if he would stand in Nice for general elections also due early next year but added: "It's not impossible."
Electricity was cut off at the beginning of the meeting, forcing Le Pen to speak in near-darkness for close to an hour.
"It would be very surprising if this was not sabotage. But I expect a series of such incidents in the electoral campaign leading to 1998," he said.
Before and during the conference, several thousand people demonstrated nearby in a protest called by leftist parties and anti-racism groups to denounce Le Pen's visit.

The National Front's anti-immigration stance has been pushed to the top of the political agenda by controversy over a bill sponsored by the centre-right government to close remaining loopholes in existing immigration laws.
